inputs.original_text: Even five months after the ceasefire was announced in Gaza, the airstrikes have not stopped and the humanitarian situation keeps deteriorating, with life growing darker and harsher for the people there. This reflects deep structural inequalities, historical patterns of injustice, and the failure to protect vulnerable communities from displacement and ongoing violence. A 56-year-old father of five named Ahmed Baroud, now displaced in Deir al-Balah, described it by saying, “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” Rather than blaming those suffering for the crisis, the focus must be on addressing root causes through institutional reform, social justice, and safeguards for families and workers caught in the crossfire.
inputs.modified_text: Even five months after the ceasefire was announced in Gaza, the airstrikes continue unchecked and the humanitarian crisis is only worsening, making life increasingly dark and harsh for the people on the ground. This is yet another manifestation of deep structural inequalities and historical patterns of injustice that have long failed to shield vulnerable communities from displacement and relentless violence. A 56-year-old father of five named Ahmed Baroud, now displaced in Deir al-Balah, captured it clearly: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” We cannot blame those caught in the suffering. Instead, the priority must be confronting the root causes through institutional reform, social justice, and real protections for the families and workers trapped in this crossfire.
